name: filing_sim
hypothesis: Firms that rewrite much of their 10-K vs last year's (low similarity) earn lower future returns: managers change disclosures when news (often bad) arrives, investors rarely compare filings side by side, so prices adjust slowly over months. For ASAM (long-only): a screen of stocks to avoid.
definition: Cosine similarity (word counts) between a firm's original 10-K and its most recent original 10-K filed 9-15 months earlier (WRDS bow_cossim, lookback 1-4, amendments skipped). Low = changer. Monthly value = latest with published_date <= month-end, at most 15 months old.
source: WRDS SEC Analytics Suite, wrdssec.bow_cossim (Bag of Words); linked via wrdssec.wciklink_gvkey and CRSP-Compustat (ccmxpf_lnkhist)
citation: Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen (2020), Lazy Prices, Journal of Finance 75(3), 1371ff., doi:10.1111/jofi.12885
inputs_required: 10-K text similarity (cosine), SEC acceptance date and time, EDGAR filing date, CIK-gvkey link, CCM link, NYSE trading days
timing_rule: exact: SEC acceptance time (New York) at or before 4 p.m. -> same trading day; after 4 p.m. or no time -> next trading day; acceptance date after the EDGAR filing date (WRDS re-processing date, mostly 1994-2002) -> EDGAR filing date, next trading day
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Usable from 1998 (EDGAR phase-in); last filings 2024-12, so 2025 values are 2024 10-Ks. Column format_change_2010_14 flags values from 10-Ks published 2010-2014: a filing-format change tripled 10-K length; in 2010-2012 the largest firms were 57-63% of the bottom fifth (English-only cosine_eng did not fix it). Paper's sample ends 2014 -> 2015-2024 is out of sample. Process and decisions: signals/lazy_prices/progress.md.
